top.line: Who insures agents, and how a new insurer would start
top.para: Several companies sell AI agent cover, but none we found prices per row of a behaviour policy. The industry has every part such a company needs. Capital is a carrier's business, so the first one starts as a managing agent on someone else's capital, small, and earns its record.

in-short.line: Eight lines from the pieces to the providers
in-short.para: We have the pieces; AIUC, Armilla, Testudo, Munich Re and Harbor sell cover; the industry separates the parts; neobanks were a licence problem more than capital; for a carrier capital is the business; start as an MGA; cover already lapses on unpatched CVEs; start small, then providers.

have.line: The policy, the mapping and the formula exist
have.para: The open behaviour policy, the AIUC-1 standard as a graph on sgit.ai, and a deterministic formula give a premium and a payout for an agent. The questions now are practical: who sells this, and what a company that did would need, built by insurance experts with capital.

landscape.line: Five companies sell agent cover; none per row
landscape.para: AIUC pairs a standard and audits with cover and raised a Series A in September 2026; Armilla and Testudo write it at Lloyd's with limits up to $25 million and $9.25 million; Munich Re prices model performance; Harbor distributes. None prices per row of a behaviour policy.

chain.line: Evidence, pricing, the balance sheet, reinsurance
chain.para: A managing agent or coverholder prices and binds under a binding authority without carrying the risk; a carrier or Lloyd's syndicate holds the capital; fronting carriers wrote over $22 billion in 2025; reinsurers take the tail. Claims on rows can be close to parametric.

capital.line: Neobanks needed a licence; carriers need capital
capital.para: E-money firms need €350,000 and cannot lend safeguarded money; banks hold capital mostly against credit risk, 77.9% in the EU. For an insurer, capital covers a one-in-two-hundred-year year, with a UK floor of £2.4 million. Capped rows make the worst year easier to bound.

path.line: Coalition and At-Bay bought carriers once they had books
path.para: Coalition acquired a carrier in August 2022 and At-Bay in January 2023, taking on balance-sheet risk. Lemonade, a full carrier, still cedes about 18% of premium. So start with several companies, a managing agent among them; large insurers may build the same divisions.

small.line: Small agents, QA and a few per cent of users first
small.para: Low limits on niche agents, agents in QA, or 1% to 5% of users give a carrier bounded exposure and the new company a loss record. Lloyd's Lab backs an AI risk engine; Deloitte projected $4.7 billion of AI premiums by 2032.

fractal.line: Many small policies; cover lapses on unpatched CVEs
fractal.para: A company-wide policy aggregates one per agent, tied to where it runs. A PHP site stays insured only while no known vulnerability is left unpatched: Chubb shifts risk after a 45-day grace period, and another insurer excludes CVSS above 8 after three weeks.

providers.line: Providers may insure their own agents; it may be required
providers.para: OpenAI considered self-insurance and secured up to $300 million of cover; Anthropic partly uses its own funds for settlements. Motor insurance is compulsory; the European Parliament asked for similar cover for high-risk AI in 2020, a resolution that does not bind.

questions.para: Who would grant a binding authority, how much capital capped rows need, how correlated losses across one model work, what a claim looks like, who certifies runtimes, where providers' warranties sit, and which market goes first.

limits.line: Not an expert's plan; the landscape as found
limits.para: Building this needs insurance experts; the landscape is what was found publicly; the capital comparison is simplified; the precedents are cyber; the forecast is Deloitte's from 2024; no law requiring agent insurance was found.

sources.line: Dinis's memo, checked by a research agent
sources.para: The second memo of the series; the neobank correction came from the research. Every source was fetched on 28 October 2026 and linked where used; the research notes record what could not be verified.
